items.title: A mole of marshmallows would cover the USA 600 miles deep
items.claim: 6.022 times 10 to the 23 is just a number until you try to picture it. Avogadro's number of marshmallows would bury the entire surface of the United States to a depth of 600 miles.
items.prompt: Roughly how many moles of water molecules are in a single drop (about 0.05 mL)?

options.text: About 0.003 moles, which is roughly 1.7 times 10 to the 21 molecules
Around 6 times 10 to the 23 — one drop is one mole
About 0.05 moles, the same as the volume in millilitres

items.reveal_title: Even a microscopic drop contains stupefying numbers of molecules
items.reveal:
0.05 mL of water has a mass of 0.05 g. Water is 18 g per mole, so 0.05 / 18 equals about 0.0028 mol. Multiply by Avogadro's number and you get roughly 1.7 times 10 to the 21 molecules.

If you counted those molecules at one per second, it would take about 50 trillion years — over 3000 times the age of the universe. Chemistry is the study of mind-bending counts of incredibly tiny things.
items.why: The mole is treated as a unit conversion when it should be treated as a stark statement about scale.

items.title: More than 99 percent of the visible universe is in a state not taught at GCSE
items.claim: Solid, liquid, gas — the three states of matter on the syllabus. But more than 99 percent of normal matter in the universe (stars, ionised interstellar medium) is plasma — a hot ionised gas with free electrons and ions.
items.prompt: What makes plasma a separate state of matter from a hot gas?

options.text: Plasma is denser than a gas
In plasma the atoms have been ionised so electrons and ions move independently; the substance conducts electricity, responds strongly to electric and magnetic fields, and emits its own light
Plasma is hotter only in name
Plasma is gas that has been compressed

items.reveal:
Heat any gas above a few thousand kelvin and electrons start to break free from atoms. The collection of free electrons and ions is a plasma. Stars, lightning, neon signs, fluorescent lamps and the auroras are all plasmas.

Because charges are free, plasmas have collective behaviours that gases lack: they conduct electricity, they pinch and twist under their own magnetic fields, they support waves that no gas can carry. Magnetohydrodynamics is the whole branch of physics that deals with their flow.

Fusion energy research (ITER, JET, tokamaks) depends on confining hydrogen plasma at over 100 million K with magnetic fields. The plasma cannot touch any wall — the wall would vaporise long before the plasma cooled.
items.why: The 'three states' are good for Earth-surface chemistry. Cosmically, plasma is the default.
